title: Romanian Media Spotlight: PubTV and Turnul Chindiei Feature Green Horizon
summary: Prominent regional news portals PubTV Romania and Turnul Chindiei publish in-depth features on Green Horizon, highlighting how young people harnessed camera drones, digital storytelling, and international cooperation for climate mitigation.
full_text:
The Green Horizon project has received prominent television and press coverage in Romania following the successful rollout of the national dissemination conference and youth media exhibitions.

Media outlet PubTV Romania published a dedicated report titled "Green Horizon: Tinerii, tehnologia și creativitatea pentru un viitor mai verde" (Green Horizon: Youth, technology, and creativity for a greener future), spotlighting the innovative pedagogical model where youth from Germany, Romania, and Türkiye were trained not merely as passive observers, but as aerial photographers and environmental storytellers equipped with cutting-edge drone cameras.

Simultaneously, leading regional publication Turnul Chindiei featured the project under the headline "Green Horizon: Tehnologie și educație pentru mediu" (Green Horizon: Technology and education for the environment). The article emphasizes the project’s transnational synergies between coordinator Integrational e.V. (Bonn, Germany), lead media partner Asociația Empower Plus (Brașov, Romania), and environmental expert partner Yenilikçi Eğitim Bilim ve Sanat Derneği (Mersin, Türkiye).

Both media publications highlighted the open educational availability of all project outcomes—including the 3-chapter Educational Booklet, the youth documentary series, and the interactive 3D Virtual Reality exhibition—all released as Open Educational Resources under Creative Commons CC BY-SA 4.0 license.

On Instagram, official posts documented the evolution of participants—from crafting homemade pinhole cameras during the Brașov training course to piloting quadcopters over coastal wetlands in Mersin and riverbanks along the Rhine. On Facebook, partner organizations shared public updates engaging educational institutions, local municipalities, and European youth networks. These posts disseminated workshop announcements, screened short teaser reels from the youth documentary series, and celebrated the release of the Open Educational Resource booklet.

title: Newsletter No. 3: What We Achieved — Dissemination Conferences, Final Partner Meeting & Global VR Launch
summary: Issue No. 3 celebrates project culmination: 3 national multiplier conferences, the final evaluation meeting in Mersin, our global 3D VR exhibition launch, and project impact metrics.
full_text:
The consortium is proud to publish the third issue of the official Green Horizon Newsletter, titled "WHAT WE ACHIEVED (Progress May – October 2026)".

In July 2026, Green Horizon went fully public across Europe. Three national dissemination conferences presented the youth documentary series and curated photography exhibitions to young people, youth workers, and local institutional representatives:
• 17 July 2026 in Romania: Asociația Empower Plus presented the whole journey from the Brașov training course to local workshops, screening photos and videos.
• 22 July 2026 in Mersin, Türkiye: IESA convened 20 participants, including teachers and municipal representatives, exploring drone and video integration into grassroots climate action.
• 25 July 2026 in Bonn, Germany: Integrational e.V. hosted 20 attendees, closing the circle in the city where the partnership began.

On 31 July – 1 August 2026, coordinators met in Mersin for the Final Transnational Partner Meeting, adopting a comprehensive sustainability agreement to ensure all educational resources, films, and websites remain accessible indefinitely.

Since October 2026, the 3D Virtual Reality exhibition is live online on Artsteps and MetaSteps, featuring dedicated country rooms for Germany, Romania, and Türkiye with a fully guided audio-visual tour.

Green Horizon in Numbers:
• 18 youth workers trained as certified drone mentors
• 60 young people trained across local workshops
• 3 short documentary films produced
• 3 dissemination conferences organized
• 1 open Educational Booklet under CC BY-SA 4.0

The consortium extends sincere gratitude to all youth participants, partner teams at Integrational e.V., Empower Plus, and IESA, and the German National Agency JUGEND für Europa.

title: Newsletter No. 2: Local Voices From Above — 60 Young People Take Drone Controls Across Three Cities
summary: Issue No. 2 follows trained youth workers stepping into trainer roles across Mersin, Bonn, and Brașov, empowering 60 young participants to document local environmental stress.
full_text:
The partnership has published Issue No. 2 of the official Green Horizon Newsletter, titled "LOCAL VOICES FROM ABOVE (Progress November 2025 – April 2026)".

In April 2026, trained youth workers transitioned into trainers. Each partner organization ran an intensive one-day workshop for 20 young people in their home city—60 young people in total—most taking control of a camera drone and video editing suite for the first time:

• 19 April 2026 · Mersin, Türkiye ("From chaos to order"): IESA kicked off the series. Following an orientation to Turkish drone regulations, participants mastered cutting, transitions, and narrative structuring. Focus areas included Mediterranean warming (accelerating faster than global averages), extreme heatwaves, and seasonal drought stress on local delta wetlands.

• 23 April 2026 · Bonn, Germany ("The Rhine and the city"): Integrational e.V. welcomed 20 youth in Bonn. Participants mapped city climate impacts, including severe low water levels on the Rhine (recalling dry summers of 2018 and 2022 when cargo barges sailed half-empty) and urban heat islands, while navigating Bonn’s restricted airspace protocols.

• 29 April 2026 · Brașov, Romania ("Filming with drones"): Empower Plus trained 20 young participants in Romanian. Sessions covered drone flight dynamics, camera movement parameters, and a structured 4-step editing pipeline: import, cutting and rhythm, colour grading, and export.

Across all three cities, the identical 4-stage pedagogical flow (Learn, fly, film, edit) yielded three finished short documentary videos and the core photography collection.

title: Newsletter No. 1: Green Horizon Takes Off — From Bonn Kick-off to Brașov Training Course
summary: The inaugural issue details the foundation of our transnational consortium, pinhole camera optics experiments, EU 120m drone safety rules, and flight practice in Brașov.
full_text:
We are thrilled to present the inaugural issue of the Green Horizon Newsletter: "GREEN HORIZON TAKES OFF (Progress May – October 2025)".

What does climate change look like from 120 metres up? Green Horizon set out to answer that question with youth workers and young people from Germany, Romania, and Türkiye. With drones, cameras, and editing apps, participants learn to document what is changing in their own regions and turn observations into compelling stories that inspire civic action.

Three Organisations, One Horizon (1 May 2025 – 31 August 2026):
• Integrational e.V. (Bonn, Germany) coordinates the project, bringing proven expertise in engaging young people with migrant backgrounds.
• Asociația Empower Plus (Brașov, Romania) leads drone piloting, aerial photography, and digital media production.
• Yenilikçi Eğitim Bilim ve Sanat Derneği - IESA (Mersin, Türkiye) spearheads environmental education and authorship of the Educational Booklet.

The Kick-Off Meeting (28–29 July 2025 · Bonn, Germany):
Partner teams convened in Bonn to finalize activity schedules, establish communication and dissemination matrices, confirm strict EU visibility rules, and prepare the Brașov training course.

Training Course in Brașov (11–18 October 2025 · 18 Youth Workers · 6 Days):
Six youth workers from each country gathered in Brașov for an immersive week. Participants began by crafting pinhole cameras from recycled containers to grasp foundational optical physics, mastered EU "open" category drone regulations (including the mandatory 120-metre ceiling and pilot line-of-sight constraints), conducted outdoor aerial filming drills, and edited environmental documentaries, culminating in Youthpass certification.

title: Green Horizon Virtual Exhibition Goes Live Online on MetaSteps and Artsteps
summary: The digital 3D virtual reality exhibition goes live online ahead of the national dissemination conferences, welcoming visitors worldwide to explore aerial climate perspectives on MetaSteps and Artsteps.
full_text:
Ahead of the summer multiplier conferences, the Green Horizon partnership launched its immersive 3D Virtual Reality Exhibition online.

Hosted on Artsteps and MetaSteps, the virtual exhibition features drone photography and video installations capturing the Rhine riverbed in Germany, Carpathian forest ecosystems surrounding Brașov, and Mediterranean coastal deltas in Mersin. The virtual space is structured into three dedicated country wings and includes an automated guided tour, background environmental narratives, and interactive hotspots accessible from mobile browsers, desktop PCs, and VR headsets without requiring specialized software.

The virtual launch ensures that the artistic and educational contributions of participating youth reach audiences worldwide, providing a permanent digital showcase for European climate awareness.

title: Final Transnational Partner Meeting Held in Mersin, Türkiye
summary: Consortium delegations from Germany, Romania, and Türkiye convened in Mersin on 31 July – 1 August 2026 to review evaluation metrics, verify EU visibility, and adopt the long-term sustainability agreement.
full_text:
On 31 July – 1 August 2026, 9 project coordinators and lead trainers representing Integrational e.V., Asociația Empower Plus, and Yenilikçi Eğitim Bilim ve Sanat Derneği (IESA) gathered in Mersin, Türkiye for the Final Transnational Partner Meeting.

Over two intensive days, the consortium conducted qualitative and quantitative evaluations of all 7 project activities:
1. A1 Project Management & Kick-off Meeting in Bonn
2. A2 Transnational Training Course in Brașov
3. A3 Educational Booklet authorship and release
4. A4 Grassroots youth workshops in Mersin, Bonn, and Brașov
5. A5 Youth documentary series production and curated photo exhibition
6. A6 Dedicated project website and 3D Virtual Reality gallery
7. A7 Multiplier dissemination conferences and final partner review

The partners signed the formal Sustainability Agreement, guaranteeing that all web infrastructure, educational booklets, photo archives, and video links will remain hosted online and free to access for a minimum of five years. Discussions also initiated conceptual frameworks for subsequent Erasmus+ climate literacy collaborations.

• 23 April 2026: Bonn, Germany (Integrational e.V.) — 20 youth

A total of 60 young people, many of whom had never handled a drone controller or edited video footage, received hands-on flight instructions, safety guidance, and smartphone editing training. Participants investigated environmental conditions in their own neighbourhoods—from coastal erosion in Mersin to urban heat and low water levels on the Rhine in Bonn, and protected forest reserves near Brașov—generating raw footage that formed the backbone of the project documentary films.

title: Educational Booklet on Drone Operation, Photography and Climate Change Released as CC BY-SA 4.0 Open Resource
summary: The consortium published its tri-lingual Educational Booklet, offering 3 comprehensive chapters covering flight safety checklists, photographic framing, and environmental education under CC BY-SA 4.0.
full_text:
The Green Horizon consortium has officially published the "Booklet on Drone Operation, Photography and Effective Ways to Mitigate Climate Change".

Crafted under the editorial leadership of IESA with collaborative input from Integrational e.V. and Asociația Empower Plus, the booklet serves as a practical handbook for youth workers, school educators, and young leaders. The publication is structured into three core chapters:
1. Climate Change Context & Youth Action: Understanding local environmental indicators, European Green Deal goals, and civic participation.
2. Photography & Cinematography Fundamentals: Lighting, rule of thirds, framing, storytelling, and ethical visual documentation.
3. Safe Drone Operation & Regulations: EU flight rules, airspace verification, weather risk assessment, battery management, and practical flight checklists.

The booklet is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-SA 4.0) and is available for free digital download in English, German, and Romanian.

title: Intensive 6-Day Training Course in Brașov: 18 Youth Workers Master Drone Technology and Environmental Storytelling
summary: 18 youth workers from Germany, Romania, and Türkiye met in Brașov on 11–18 October 2025, progressing from handmade pinhole cameras to advanced drone cinematography and EU safety rules.
full_text:
From 11 to 18 October 2025, Asociația Empower Plus hosted 18 youth workers (6 from Germany, 6 from Romania, and 6 from Türkiye) in Brașov, Romania for an intensive 6-day training mobility.

Designed to bridge technology and environmental pedagogy, the course guided participants through progressive experiential modules:
• Analog Optics: Participants constructed working pinhole cameras from recycled tin cans and cardboard, developing an intuitive understanding of focal length, exposure, and light capture.
• EU Regulations & Flight Safety: Trainers instructed youth workers on European Union "open" category restrictions, emphasizing the 120-metre legal ceiling, pilot line-of-sight mandates, and emergency fail-safe procedures.
• Practical Flight Drills: In designated open park spaces, participants practiced flight maneuvers, obstacle navigation, gimbal control, and cinematic tracking.
• Post-Production: Teams edited aerial footage into short climate vignettes using mobile and open-source desktop editing suites.

All 18 participants successfully completed the mobility, evaluated their learning through the European Youthpass framework, and received certificates qualifying them to lead local youth workshops.

title: Consortium Launches Project with Kick-Off Meeting in Bonn, Germany
summary: 9 coordinators from Integrational e.V., Asociația Empower Plus, and IESA gathered in Bonn on 28–29 July 2025 to align project management and timeline milestones.
full_text:
On 28–29 July 2025, delegations from the three partner organizations convened in Bonn, Germany for the official Transnational Kick-Off Meeting of the Green Horizon project.

Coordinated by Integrational e.V., the 9 participating project leaders finalized operational protocols for the 16-month initiative (1 May 2025 – 31 August 2026, project number 2024-3-DE04-KA210-YOU-000293009). Discussions established risk monitoring matrices, budgetary oversight rules, and strict adherence to European Union visibility guidelines.

The partners formalized preparation deadlines for Activity A2 (the Brașov training course), established the editorial roadmap for Activity A3 (the Educational Booklet), and agreed on a shared communication strategy spanning social media, regional press outreach, and official newsletters.
